name: Norval Foundation
funding: Property investor Louis Norval financed it entirely at the 2018 opening and set up a capital fund. Sponsors include Schroders (art prize), Stonehage Fleming (2021 auction) and Sanlam.
watch: Art centre in Steenberg, Cape Town, and custodian of the Gerard Sekoto Foundation. Funded by a philanthropic endowment for African modern and contemporary art.
records_note: It names its twelve trustees on the About page but posts no annual reports, accounts or funder list.

name: NTT InterCommunication Center (ICC)
funding: Corporate cultural facility (2026) run and paid for by NTT East, a telecom operator, in Tokyo Opera City Tower.
watch: Opened in 1997 to mark the centenary of Japan's telephone service. A non-profit art and science venue, not a commercial attraction.
records_note: ICC publishes nothing itself; its operator NTT East posts annual financial results and names its directors, and ICC lists no funders.

name: OCAT Shenzhen
funding: Founded 2005 and owned by OCT Group, a central state-owned tourism and property group. OCT cut funding sharply in 2023 to venue costs only; OCAT must earn its own income.
watch: Beijing, Shanghai and Xi'an venues were suspended in 2022 and their work moved here. OCAT Shanghai closed in 2021 after a video outcry.
records_note: The official site blocks automated access with a Cloudflare check, so reports, accounts, funders and board could not be checked; searches found none of them.

name: Palais de Lomé
funding: Togolese state paid the XOF 2.2bn renovation and funds operations. Director Sonia Lawson sought sponsors in 2019. CFAO and Toyota Tsusho hosted an award show in June 2026.
watch: No censorship, cancelled show or protest found.
records_note: No reports, accounts or board are published; the patrons thank-you page says its content will be available soon.

name: Pallant House Gallery
funding: £3.0M income (FY2025). Chichester District Council £130k a year to 2030, Fidelity Foundation £260k, Art Fund, patrons and bequests; Dreweatts, Evelyn Partners, Sofas & Stuff. No regular Arts Council grant.
watch: Accredited museum operating under the Museums Association Code of Ethics.
records_note: One annual review (2022-23) is online; accounts 2021 to 2025 are on the Charity Commission register; corporate partners show as logos; the board is listed.

name: PHI Foundation
funding: Greenberg family (Minto real estate fortune). Federal and Quebec governments committed C$26.6M in 2022 for the PHI contemporain expansion. Programming is free.
watch: Contemporary art foundation in Old Montreal offering free public exhibitions.
records_note: Publishes no annual report, accounts or board list; the Partners Circle page shows six undated corporate logos, launched in 2025.

name: Pinto Art Museum
funding: Private museum founded in 2010 to show the collection of physician and patron Dr. Joven Cuanang. Run by the non-profit Silangan Foundation; entry is ticketed.
watch: Complex designed by artist Antonio Leaño.
records_note: The museum site publishes no annual report, accounts, donor list or board; it names only its founder, Dr. Joven Cuanang.

name: Pivô
funding: Federal Cultural Incentive Law (Lei Rouanet), philanthropic patron circle, international cultural foundations. Independent Brazilian non-profit audit.
watch: Independent space of 3,500m² inside Oscar Niemeyer's Copan Building in downtown São Paulo. Runs site-specific commissions, the Pivô Pesquisa research residency and public debates.

name: Plug In ICA
funding: Canada Council, Manitoba Arts Council, Winnipeg Arts Council and the federal government. Corporate supporters: RBC Foundation and Johnston Group, a benefits firm.
watch: First non-profit Institute of Contemporary Art in Canada.
records_note: Lists its board and names members and supporters on a 2025-26 recognition page; sponsor logos are undated, and no annual reports or accounts are posted.

name: Project Arts Centre
funding: The Arts Council / An Chomhairle Ealaíon, Dublin City Council, non-commercial ticket sales. Registered Charity No. 20008447.
watch: Multidisciplinary contemporary arts institute in Temple Bar.

name: Pulitzer Arts Foundation
watch: 501(c)(3) private operating foundation in St. Louis, in a building designed by Tadao Ando.
records_note: No annual reports or donor list on its site; 990-PF filings for 2001 to 2023 are on ProPublica, and the board is listed.
